title: BECE Business Studies: Office Practice - Business Studies - Office Procedure
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The established sequence of steps, methods, or rules designed to ensure that routine administrative tasks are performed correctly is known as
questions.explain: **Office procedure** refers to the agreed and established sequence of steps for carrying out standard clerical and administrative operations.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is the main importance of having an established office procedure in an organization?
options: It makes it easier for employees to come to work late.
It allows the manager to travel abroad on holidays.
It ensures consistency, uniformity, and efficiency in handling tasks.
It drastically increases the cost of raw materials.
questions.explain: A key importance of office procedure is that it provides a standard way of working, which **ensures consistency, uniformity, and efficiency**, reducing confusion and errors.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A commercial document prepared by a seller and sent to a buyer, detailing the goods supplied and the total amount to be paid, is an
questions.explain: An **invoice** is drawn up by the seller showing the items, quantity, price, and terms of sale. It serves as a bill demanding payment from the buyer.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The appropriate document issued as a written acknowledgment that payment for a product or service has been received is a
questions.explain: A **receipt** confirms that money has exchanged hands and serves as proof of payment.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When preparing a commercial bill or invoice, the gross total is calculated by
options: subtracting the unit price from the quantity
multiplying the quantity of goods by the unit price
dividing the quantity of goods by the discount
adding the unit price to the discount
questions.explain: The standard procedure for billing requires calculating the value of the items by **multiplying the quantity of goods by the unit price** (i.e., $\text{Quantity} \times \text{Unit Price} = \text{Total}$).
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A written instruction directed to a bank, asking it to pay a specific sum of money to the person named on the document, is called a
questions.explain: A **cheque** is an unconditional order in writing, drawn on a banker, signed by the drawer, directing the bank to pay a certain sum of money on demand.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following payment methods is drawn by a bank on its own head office or branch, thereby guaranteeing payment to the payee?
questions.explain: Unlike a personal cheque which can bounce, a **Bank draft** is a cheque drawn by a bank on itself or its own funds, guaranteeing the payment to the recipient.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Paying for office supplies via a Point of Sale (POS) terminal or internet banking portal is classified as
questions.explain: **E-payment** (Electronic payment) encompasses paying for goods or services on the internet, via POS, USSD, or other electronic media without exchanging physical cash.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Payment by which of the following means involves the physical exchange of currency notes and is highly risky for settling very large business transactions?
questions.explain: Payment by **Cash** involves giving physical legal tender notes and coins. Due to risks of theft and counting errors, it is not recommended for large business amounts.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The petty cashier is given a monthly float of $₦15,000$. If the total expenditure for the month is $₦12,000$, what is the closing Imprest balance?
questions.explain: The balance is determined by subtracting total expenses from the initial float: $$\text{Balance} = \text{Float} - \text{Expenses}$$ $$\text{Balance} = 15,000 - 12,000 = 3,000$$.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Using the figures from the previous scenario (Float = $₦15,000$; Spent = $₦12,000$), what exact amount is required for the restoration (reimbursement) of the Imprest at the beginning of the next month?
questions.explain: Under the imprest system, restoration (reimbursement) restores the balance back to the original float. Therefore, the exact amount spent is what gets reimbursed. $$\text{Restoration Amount} = \text{Amount Spent} = ₦12,000$$.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In a business organization, the specific room or area where raw materials and finished goods are safely kept until they are needed is the
questions.explain: A **store** (or warehouse) is a designated space for safely keeping stock, raw materials, or finished goods prior to use or sale.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Documents like bin cards, store ledgers, and goods received notes are used to keep track of the movement of goods. These are broadly called
questions.explain: **Store records** are specialized documents kept by the storekeeper to maintain accurate details of the quantity, quality, and values of materials stored.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The entire process of sourcing, ordering, purchasing, and receiving essential materials required by a business is referred to as
questions.explain: **Procurement** is the formal business procedure of acquiring or purchasing supplies, equipment, and services needed to operate.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the standard procedure for store procurement, which document does a department head use to formally ask the purchasing department to buy needed supplies?
questions.explain: A **Purchase requisition form** initiates the procurement procedure. It is an internal document used to request the purchasing department to buy specific items.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The process of physically counting and valuing all the goods currently held in a store at a particular date is known as
questions.explain: **Stock taking** (or inventory counting) is the manual verification of physical goods in the store to ensure they match the recorded figures.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: One primary importance of regular stock taking in an organization is to
options: increase the cost of the goods
eliminate the need for a store clerk
questions.explain: Stock taking ensures transparency by comparing physical items with store records, which is critical for **discovering discrepancies, damages, shortages, or internal theft**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which document is usually sent along with transported goods to enable the receiver to verify the quantity and description of the items delivered?
questions.explain: A **Delivery note** accompanies the physical goods and lists the quantities and details, serving as proof that the goods arrived correctly when signed by the receiver.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A physical document signed by an authorized manager that allows a driver or dispatcher to move corporate items or products out of the factory premises is a
questions.explain: A **Gate pass** is a security and store document giving official authorization for goods or assets to be taken out of the company gates.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a modern recognized procedure for effecting business payments?
questions.explain: The syllabus outlines modern business payments as Cash, Bank transfer, Cheque, Bank draft, and E-payment. **Barter trading** (exchanging goods for goods) is an ancient system, not a modern office payment procedure.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An invoice is fundamentally drawn up by the __________ and sent to the __________.
questions.explain: Because it is a bill requesting payment for goods supplied, an invoice is always initiated and drawn up by the **seller** and presented to the **buyer**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In handling minor office expenditures, the fixed initial sum of money given to a petty cashier to start a period is called the
questions.explain: The **imprest float** is the pre-agreed base amount of cash assigned to the petty cashier to run small, daily expenses like stamps, tea, and cleaning items.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A customer wishing to pay for bulk goods without issuing a physical cheque can electronically move the exact funds straight into the company's account via a
questions.explain: A **Bank transfer** allows for the electronic routing of funds directly from the buyer's account to the seller's account without a paper cheque.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When receiving goods into the store, the storekeeper typically compares the items brought by the supplier's driver with both the supplier's Delivery Note and the organization's
questions.explain: To ensure they aren't accepting unordered goods, the storekeeper cross-checks the delivery note against a copy of the **Local Purchase Order (LPO)**, which proves the company actually ordered the items.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A severe lack of proper office procedures regarding payments and receipts in an organization will most likely lead to
questions.explain: Without established rules for drafting invoices, accepting cash, or storing goods, there will be no accountability, directly resulting in **errors, fraud, and financial confusion**.
questions.subject: Business Studies
